articles.title: Cameron Myers shines in star-studded field to win 1500m at Diamond League final
articles.summary: Australian beats Olympic champs Jakob Ingebrigtsen and Cole Hocker. Pole vaulter Kurtis Marschall soars over 5.82m to finish third in Brussels. Middle-distance runner Cameron Myers has become only the eighth Australian to win a Diamond League final crown with victory in the men’s 1500m in Brussels.
body: The 20-year-old claimed one of the biggest wins of his career to date as he beat a star-studded field that included Olympic champions Jakob Ingebrigtsen and Cole Hocker to continue his own meteoric rise.
Myers timed a late burst down the home straight to perfection and dipped at the line to snatch victory in 3:30.14 ahead of Kenya’s Phanuel Kipkosgei Koech (3:30.18).
Ingebrigtsen, on the comeback trail after Achilles surgery in February, dictated the pace of the race and looked on course for a morale-boosting win before ​ tiring in the last 30 metres.
America’s Ethan Strand edged past the Norwegian in the final few steps to cross the line in 3:30.50 and round out the podium.

articles.title: José Mourinho sick as a Parrott as Real Madrid sunk by Real Betis and Irish supersub
articles.summary: Mbappé sees late penalty saved by Valles. PSG are beaten by league leaders Monaco. Real Madrid’s perfect start in La Liga ⁠ended on Friday when Real Betis beat them 1-0, with the ⁠substitute Troy Parrott ⁠scoring ​nine minutes from time and goalkeeper Álvaro Valles saving a stoppage-time ⁠penalty…
body: The clash began at a high tempo but the pace ⁠dropped after the interval in the heat in ​Seville. The Republic of Ireland star Parrott, introduced ‌in the 68th ‌minute, broke the deadlock in the 81st when ‌he reacted quickly after Thibaut Courtois parried a header into his path.

Mbappé struck the crossbar four minutes later before the substitute Carlos Espí met a cross from Vinícius Júnior with a spectacular bicycle kick, only for the equaliser to be ruled ​out for offside following a VAR review.
Nelson Deossa then nearly sealed the victory for hosts Betis with a long-range effort after spotting Courtois ⁠off his line, but the goalkeeper recovered to ​make ​the save.

José Mourinho’s Madrid got one ​final opportunity when Natan brought down ​Vinícius inside ‌the area, ​deep ​into stoppage time, but Valles saved Mbappé’s spot-kick to preserve Betis’s lead and secure the three points.

articles.title: Improving Alcaraz underlines title credentials in wide-open draw
articles.summary: Defending champion Carlos Alcaraz underlines his US Open title credentials by sweeping aside Wu Yibing to reach the fourth round as the draw opens up further.
body: Carlos Alcaraz swept Wu Yibing aside to reach the US Open fourth round - and said he is getting better with every match as he continues his return from a long-term injury lay-off.
The Spaniard underlined why he remains a serious contender to defend his title in New York with a 6-3 6-4 6-1 victory over China's Wu.
The 23-year-old's opening-round match in Flushing Meadows was his first on a singles court for 139 days after injuring his wrist in April.
Alcaraz came through his opener in straight sets but had to battle back from a set down against Portugal's Jaime Faria in the second round.

articles.title: USL and players ratify new CBA, raising salaries and introducing 12-month deals
articles.summary: New pact includes terms for first-division USL Premier. Base pay for Championship grows from $31k to $42k. Agreement runs through the 2030 season. The United Soccer League and USL Players Association announced the ratification of a new collective bargaining agreement for two levels of the…
body: Among the headline items of the deals is the introduction of 12-month contracts for players, a codified first in the US lower divisions. The first USL CBAs worked to standardize 10-month contracts; before then, clubs varied in their commitments to players. Championship players will earn a base compensation (which includes housing) of $42,000 in 2026 – up from $31,000 – with that floor increasing annually over the term of the agreement. The USL Premier will also launch with 12-month contracts and a compensation floor of $67,500 in 2028 with annual increases worked into the CBA.

“This collective bargaining agreement is a significant step forward for the USL and our players and reflects the shared commitment on both sides to continue growing the game and advancing professional standards,” USL president and CEO Paul McDonough said in a statement. “It provides long-term stability for our players, clubs and leagues, and greater confidence to invest in the future of the USL.”

articles.title: ‘Someone is smoking weed’: Sabalenka halts US Open match due to cannabis smell
articles.summary: ‘It’s tricky to handle when you’re trying to compete’ Alcaraz into fourth round after straight sets victory. Aryna Sabalenka briefly stopped her match at the US Open to complain about the strong smell of cannabis on her court as she comfortably reached the fourth round in New York.
body: Sabalenka, the two-time defending champion, continued her attempts to rebuild her form as she overcame a challenging test from Kamilla Rakhimova before winning 6-3, 6-4.

Early in the match, a smiling Sabalenka approached the chair umpire Eva Asderaki-Moore while leading 3-0, stating “Someone is smoking weed, do you mind … because it’s so strong,” Afterwards, Sabalenka laughed as she described her interaction with the umpire: “I was, like, Guys, you can do whatever, you can smoke whatever, you can relax as much as you can, but please, do not do it around the tennis courts. It’s a bit tricky to handle that smell while you’re trying to compete at your best.”

articles.title: Isak finally arrives as Gakpo proves value to Liverpool
articles.summary: Has the real Alexander Isak finally arrived at Liverpool after his two-goal display in their Premier League win at Ipswich Town, asks chief football writer Phil McNulty?
body: Alexander Isak was the £125m striker who finally arrived at Liverpool by tormenting Ipswich Town - while Cody Gakpo's virtuoso performance had them giving thanks he never left.

The nuts and bolts of a comfortable Friday in Suffolk were that Liverpool won 2-0 - thanks to two Isak goals in the first nine minutes, giving them their first Premier League victory of the season and new manager Andoni Iraola's first since succeeding the sacked Arne Slot.

Liverpool 's win must be placed in the context of being against a newly promoted Ipswich Town who were game, but who shipped five goals at Manchester United last week and look ripe for the picking against attacking quality.

The wider significance, however, was that Isak finally looked like the player Liverpool broke, at that time, the British transfer record to seal an acrimonious transfer from Newcastle United last summer.

articles.title: 'It's so strong' - Sabalenka halts play over cannabis smell
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka briefly halts her US Open match against Kamilla Rakhimova because of the smell of cannabis before going on to reach the fourth round.
body: Aryna Sabalenka briefly halted her US Open match against Kamilla Rakhimova because of a strong smell of cannabis before cruising into the fourth round in New York.
Top seed Sabalenka raised the issue after going 3-0 up in the first set against Uzbekistan's Rakhimova, telling umpire Eva Asderaki-Moore that "someone is smoking weed".
Asderaki-Moore spoke to an official on her radio and made a smoking gesture to someone behind her, before play continued.
Two-time defending champion Sabalenka went on to secure a confident 6-3 6-4 victory on Louis Armstrong Stadium as she chases a fifth Grand Slam singles title.

articles.summary: There was an expectation on London City Lionesses to live up to the hype and deliver in the Women's Super League's season opener - and they did.
body: Eder Maestre's side showed they are not just a starting XI of superstars but a team who may gel quicker than many expected.
They came away from Hayes Lane, in front of a full crowd of 5,402 home fans, with an impressive 2-1 victory over Manchester United.
The scoreline could have been worse for United as London City dominated the first half and showed flashes of individual brilliance, amid a clear structure and intent.
Two-time Ballon d'Or winner Alexia Putellas made her debut and was the glue in midfield while others stole the limelight.

articles.summary: Mauricio Dubón continues to be a lethal and versatile weapon for the Atlanta Braves. Making a fairly rare start in center field for Friday’s series opener at the Philadelphia Phillies as the Braves elected to sit Michael Harris II against a left-handed starter, Dubón paid off that decision with a…
body: With the Braves clinging to a 3-2 lead after escaping a few jams where the Phillies threatened to tie the game or take the lead, Dubón followed Mike Yastrzemski’s one-out walk with a 390-foot two-run blast to left for his 11th homer of the season.
Dubón finished the night with two hits, two runs and two RBIs.

The win pushed the Braves’ record against the Phillies to 6-1 and their NL East lead to five games. It also means that if Atlanta wins one of its final six games against Philadelphia, it will hold the head-to-head tiebreaker should the teams end up tied in the standings.

articles.title: Edwin Diaz Takes Major Step Toward Dodgers Return With ‘Best’ Live Session
articles.summary: Los Angeles Dodgers reliever Edwin Diaz, who has lost the closer role until he proves otherwise, is starting to work his way back. Diaz had another live batting practice, and it was his “best one yet,” according to manager Dave Roberts.
body: Speaking to the media, including Dodgers Nation, Roberts made it clear that Diaz will need a rehab assignment before returning, and it could start sooner after his live session on Friday.
Diaz is on the injured list with neck inflammation, something that the team believes could be causing a mechanical issue.
If the minor league schedule does not work out in the Dodgers’ favor, Diaz will need to do some more live sessions before they bring him back into the bullpen fold.
Diaz will come out as a lower-leverage arm, working his way up the trust tree as things progress shortly after that, Roberts has explained in the past.

articles.title: Greaves makes more history with win at Czech Darts Open
articles.summary: Beau Greaves made more darting history as she became the first woman to win a match on the PDC's European Tour - a feat that secured her a second-round clash with Luke Humphries at the Czech Darts Open.
body: The 22-year-old rallied from 3-1 down to beat Daryl Gurney 6-4 in Prague on Friday night and will now play world No 2 Humphries in the last-32 on Saturday evening, with the winner meeting Nathan Aspinall or Andrew Gilding in round three on Sunday afternoon.

Greaves' latest landmark moment follows becoming the first woman to hit a nine-darter on the PDC Pro Tour, against Mensur Suljovic back in February, and the first to win a PDC ranking title, doing so when she edged Michael Smith 8-7 at Players Championship 11.
She was also the first woman to qualify for a European Tour event when she reached last month's Hungarian Darts Trophy.

Greaves lost to Rob Cross in the first round in Budapest despite averaging 104 but her run in Prague will now last at least one more match after pinning double one to defeat Gurney, a player she had suffered a narrow 3-2 loss to in round one of the 2026 World Championship.

articles.title: Dianna Russini’s Next NFL Move Takes Shape as Barstool Sports Emerges as Favorite
articles.summary: Dianna Russini may not be away from the NFL spotlight much longer.Five months after leaving The Athletic, Russini is “absolutely” planning a return to sports media and has been discussing several potential opportunities, according to a new report from Front Office Sports.And one possible landing…
body: And one possible landing spot has quickly separated itself from the pack.

Front Office Sports’ Michael McCarthy reported that Dave Portnoy’s Barstool Sports is currently the “lead candidate” to hire Russini as the former NFL insider plots the next chapter of her career. Russini has not made a final decision, and the report indicates she has discussed opportunities ranging from returning as a traditional NFL insider to taking on a more personality-driven role.
But if Russini ultimately lands at Barstool, it would hardly be a cold introduction.

Russini has an established relationship with Barstool, particularly “Pardon My Take” hosts Dan “Big Cat” Katz and PFT Commenter. She has appeared on the show numerous times, including during the 2026 NFL Combine in February.

articles.title: Hunt runs season's best to take third in Diamond League 200m
articles.summary: Great Britain's Amy Hunt ran a season's best in the women's 200m at the final Diamond League event of the year as she took third place in Brussels.
body: Hunt's time of 22.16 was outstripped by race winner - and reigning Olympic 100m champion - Julien Alfred of St Lucia (21.79) and America's Kayla White (22.00).
Another Brit, Success Eduan, came seventh of the eight runners after clocking 23.06 in Belgium.
Hunt was the poster girl of the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham this summer with her four gold medals and bubbly personality winning her legions of fans.
The 24-year-old topped the podium individually in the 100m and 200m in the Midlands, while she won gold as part of the women's and mixed 4x100m relays.

articles.title: How influencers at US Open are testing boundaries of tennis etiquette
articles.summary: A huge discussion around tennis etiquette has been sparked at the US Open due to the disruption caused by a growing number of content creators and influencers at Flushing Meadows.
body: The number of content creators who have been accredited to cover this year's final Grand Slam of the year has doubled from last year in a move by organisers to reach new audiences. Yet the noise and disturbance caused by them in the stands as been felt by players on court.

Chair umpire Kader Nouni admonished a group of influencers in a suite for recording a video in the middle of a point, while another incident saw a creator using the use of a bright portable ring light to take photos.
Meanwhile, in Naomi Osaka's second-round victory, chair umpire Marijana Veljovic asked fans several times to be quiet.

Some players have questioned whether the push for online engagement has gone too far with two-time champion Osaka saying: "I think obviously if you come to a sporting event, you have to respect the sport.".
